title: Config Healer: automated detection and safe remediation pipeline for data-sovereignty / retention
creator: Maya Patel
summary: Implement an operational pipeline (Config Healer) that continuously snapshots configuration for residency and retention controls, evaluates them against policy-as-code, surfaces drift, and applies safe, auditable remediation (or suggests remediations) with full evidence export for compliance reviews.
acceptance_criteria: Every tenant's residency and retention settings are snapshotted at least once per 15 minutes
Policy engine (Rego/OPA) evaluates snapshots and emits 'violation' or 'ok' with a stable schema
Autofix runbooks are configurable per policy: modes include alert-only, patch-suggested, and patch-apply-with-canary
All remediation actions produce tamper-evident evidence bundles which include before/after configs, decision reason, operator/principal, and linked PR or change event
Canary rollout path exists (10% of affected tenants) with automated rollback on failed validation or increased error rates
Console dashboard shows drift rate, remediation success rate, mean time-to-heal, and tokens cost impact
End-to-end tests validate detection -> remediation -> evidence export path in CI with simulated multi-region workloads
implementation_notes: Policy engine: adopt OPA with Rego policies stored in a Git repo (policy-catalog.git). Use versioned bundles for runtime determinism
Snapshot mechanism: lightweight config-exporter service that reads authoritative config (Config Service / DB) and emits protobuf snapshots to an append-only S3 prefix and Kafka topic
Evaluation pipeline: serverless workers consume snapshots, evaluate via OPA, and emit findings to a findings-topic (Kafka) and to the Console telemetry API
Remediation: an orchestrator (task-runner) that translates findings into patch actions using idempotent apply operations via the config API; actions are executed in stages: dry-run -> canary -> full

Safety: every auto-apply requires a signed policy version, scope-limited service account, rate limiter (max 5 patches/min globally) and a pre-apply validation step that runs model-derived and deterministic checks

Evidence: create evidence bundles as gzipped JSON with schema v1 (before, after, policy_version, evaluator_signature, operator_id, timestamp) and write to a WORM S3 bucket with lifecycle rules; register bundle UUID into Audit DB
Observability: add traces for evaluation and apply steps, emit metrics for policy latency, false-positive rate (from manual overrides), and cost delta per remediation
Fail-open/closed decision: default to 'alert-only' for new policies for 2 weeks before enabling autofix; can be overridden per-policy after security review
Integrations: push evidence bundles to customer's external compliance sink (SFTP/S3/Kafka) when tenant has external_evidence configured
Rollout: start with internal tenants in 'staging' region, expand to redwood-managed sandbox customers, then opt-in customers, then global enforcement
timeline: Week 1: infra & snapshotter; Week 2: OPA integration + policy repo; Week 3: evaluation pipeline + findings; Week 4: orchestrator + dry-run remediations; Week 5: canary, evidence export, dashboard; Week 6: QA + security review + gradual rollout
updates: 2026-02-15: Spike complete. Validated OPA Rego evaluation latency on representative snapshots (median 18ms/policy with 50 policies). --Maya
2026-02-20: Decided to use append-only snapshot storage + Kafka for near-real-time evaluation. Trade-off: slightly higher storage vs reliable replay for audit. --Liam
2026-02-28: Security review kickoff. Security asked for service account scope minimization and signed policy bundles. Added to implementation notes. --Liam
2026-03-03: Implemented evidence bundle schema v1 and wired to internal test bucket. Manual review flow created in Console for suggested patches. --Engineer: Priya Shah
2026-03-06: PM feedback: require customer-visible opt-in flag for automatic remediation. Added per-tenant enforcement toggle and per-policy mode. --PM: Carlos Ruiz

2026-03-08: QA found flakiness in canary rollback path where dependent microservice schema changes caused false negatives. Added pre-apply schema validation and service healthchecks. --QA: Janice Wong
2026-03-10: Demo to compliance showed evidence bundles satisfy 'what, when, who' requirements but requested signed evaluator digest included. Added evaluator_signature field. --Maya
test_plan: Unit tests for Rego policies using opa test harness
Integration tests: snapshot -> evaluate -> dry-run remediation in CI with mocked config-service
Chaos test: simulate delayed snapshots and ensure eventual consistency
E2E compliance test: generate evidence bundle and validate ingestion in Audit DB and external sink
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal-only (dev + staging) with alert-only mode
Phase 1: redwood-managed sandbox customers, enable suggested-patch mode
Phase 2: opt-in customers for auto-apply with canary 10%
Phase 3: global enforcement for policies marked 'regulatory' after 2-week observation and security sign-off
blockers: Security sign-off pending for auto-apply service account (ticket SEC-440)
Need infra quota for WORM S3 buckets in eu-west-1 to support tenants (ticket INF-1298)
Policy catalog needs canonicalization for retention exceptions (policy-authoring gap)
